category.name: Split Document
category.preferred_workflow: Create a deterministic source document locally, select a supported split strategy (section, heading, page, or custom range), use Document, Section, NodeImporter, or Document.ExtractPages to produce separate Document objects, and save each part with explicit file-system checks. Keep validation focused on the existence and basic integrity of the generated files.

strict_api_bans: Never reference Aspose.Words members that are absent from version 26.10.0.
Do not import or use namespaces that are not part of the official package.
canonical_patterns: Use Document, Section, NodeImporter, and HtmlSaveOptions for all splitting scenarios.
When splitting by pages, call Document.ExtractPages with zero-based start index and validated page count.
For heading-based splitting, iterate over Paragraph nodes and import the desired range into a new Document.
nullable_warning_prevention: Create all source files, folders, and streams before they are accessed.
Validate that output directories exist and are writable prior to saving split parts.

common_failure_patterns.symptom: Code references members such as DocumentSplitCriteria.SplitMode, DocumentSplitMode, or Aspose.Words.Import that do not exist in the installed library.
common_failure_patterns.cause: The example invents APIs that were never released in Aspose.Words 26.10.0.
common_failure_patterns.fix: Replace invented members with documented alternatives, for example HtmlSaveOptions.DocumentSplitCriteria and HtmlSaveOptions.DocumentSplitHeadingLevel for heading-based splitting.
common_failure_patterns.prevention: Consult the official Aspose.Words API reference for the exact class and member names before writing code.

common_failure_patterns.symptom: ExtractPages throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException because the start or end page index exceeds the document's page count.
common_failure_patterns.cause: Page numbers are calculated incorrectly or zero-based indices are mixed with one-based values.
common_failure_patterns.fix: Call Document.UpdatePageLayout() first, verify that 1 ≤ startPage ≤ endPage ≤ doc.PageCount, then invoke ExtractPages(startPage-1, pageCount).
common_failure_patterns.prevention: Always validate page numbers against the actual PageCount and use consistent zero-based indexing.

common_failure_patterns.symptom: Runtime exception reports that a new child node was created from a different document than the target.
common_failure_patterns.cause: Nodes are appended directly without using NodeImporter or cloning, violating Aspose.Words ownership rules.
common_failure_patterns.fix: Import nodes with NodeImporter (ImportFormatMode.KeepSourceFormatting) or clone them before insertion.
common_failure_patterns.prevention: Never mix nodes from different Document instances without proper import or cloning.

common_failure_patterns.symptom: CS0234 errors indicate that namespaces such as Aspose.Words.Import, Aspose.Words.Building, or Aspose.Words.Splitting cannot be found.
common_failure_patterns.cause: The code assumes the existence of non-existent sub-namespaces.
common_failure_patterns.fix: Remove invalid using directives and reference only the namespaces listed in the package documentation (e.g., Aspose.Words, Aspose.Words.Saving).
common_failure_patterns.prevention: Rely on IDE intellisense or the official documentation to determine available namespaces.

common_failure_patterns.symptom: CS1061 errors show that SaveOptions does not contain a DocumentPartSavingCallback property in the current version.
common_failure_patterns.cause: The example attempts to assign a callback to a property that was removed or never existed.
common_failure_patterns.fix: Omit the callback or implement IDocumentPartSavingCallback only where the property is supported, using the correct SaveOptions subclass.
common_failure_patterns.prevention: Verify the presence of callback properties in the specific Aspose.Words version before using them.

narrative.overview: The Split Document category demonstrates how to divide Word, HTML, EPUB, and other supported formats into smaller parts using only the native Aspose.Words 26.10.0 APIs. Verified examples show section-based splitting, heading-based manual splitting, page extraction, custom page-range extraction, and conditional format selection.
narrative.purpose: Provide an AI coding assistant with concise, version-accurate guidance for implementing reliable document-splitting workflows that rely on documented Aspose.Words classes, avoid invented APIs, and include deterministic input creation and output validation.
validation_priorities: Confirm that each expected split file exists on disk after the operation.
maintenance_notes: Review and update examples whenever a new Aspose.Words version adds or deprecates splitting-related members.
